session.question: What role did hexagonal boron nitride play in the study of canola oil as a bio-lubricant, and what details are provided about its evaluation?
session.answer:
Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) served as a solid nano-additive in canola oil-based bio-lubricants to improve tribological performance and energy efficiency. It was investigated as a sustainable lubricant modifier, alongside graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) for comparison and in mixed GNP+hBN formulations to exploit synergistic friction- and wear-reduction effects. (sikdar2021synergisticstudyof chunk 1)

The evaluation included canola oil containing 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt.% hBN nanoparticles. Dynamic viscosity was measured for these formulations, and tribological behavior was tested under boundary-lubrication conditions using pin-on-disk experiments. The measured outcomes were coefficient of friction (COF) and wear. Among the hBN concentrations, 1.0 wt.% provided the best performance, giving the lowest COF, approximately 40% below that of base canola oil. Mixed GNP+hBN lubricants reduced friction and wear even further, attributed to composite film formation and polishing effects. (sikdar2021synergisticstudyof chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-c714f967: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) was studied as a sustainable solid nano-additive in canola oil to improve its tribological performance. The paper tested canola oil with 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt.% hBN nanoparticles (along with GNP comparisons). Dynamic viscosity was measured for these formulations, and tribological performance was evaluated in the boundary-lubrication regime using pin-on-disk tests to assess coefficient of friction (COF) and wear. For hBN, 1.0 wt.% gave the lowest COF, about 40% lower than base oil. The study also formulated mixed GNP+hBN lubricants, which further reduced friction and wear.
From Soumya Sikdar, Md Hafizur Rahman, and Pradeep L. Menezes. Synergistic study of solid lubricant nano-additives incorporated in canola oil for enhancing energy efficiency and sustainability. Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su14010290, doi:10.3390/su14010290.

pqac-ee6fa9e7: The paper evaluated hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as a solid nano-additive in canola oil-based bio-lubricants at 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt.% concentrations. Tribological performance was assessed under boundary lubrication conditions using pin-on-disk tests, focusing on coefficient of friction (COF) and wear. Among the hBN samples, 1.0 wt.% produced the best result, giving the lowest COF, reported as 40% lower than base canola oil. The study also noted that combining hBN with graphene nanoplatelets in mixed formulations yielded stronger overall friction and wear reductions than either additive alone, due to composite film formation and polishing effects.
From Soumya Sikdar, Md Hafizur Rahman, and Pradeep L. Menezes. Synergistic study of solid lubricant nano-additives incorporated in canola oil for enhancing energy efficiency and sustainability. Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su14010290, doi:10.3390/su14010290.

Question: What role did hexagonal boron nitride play in the study of canola oil as a bio-lubricant, and what details are provided about its evaluation?

Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) served as a solid nano-additive in canola oil-based bio-lubricants to improve tribological performance and energy efficiency. It was investigated as a sustainable lubricant modifier, alongside graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) for comparison and in mixed GNP+hBN formulations to exploit synergistic friction- and wear-reduction effects. (sikdar2021synergisticstudyof chunk 1)

The evaluation included canola oil containing 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt.% hBN nanoparticles. Dynamic viscosity was measured for these formulations, and tribological behavior was tested under boundary-lubrication conditions using pin-on-disk experiments. The measured outcomes were coefficient of friction (COF) and wear. Among the hBN concentrations, 1.0 wt.% provided the best performance, giving the lowest COF, approximately 40% below that of base canola oil. Mixed GNP+hBN lubricants reduced friction and wear even further, attributed to composite film formation and polishing effects. (sikdar2021synergisticstudyof chunk 1)
